To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

polymer-coating of Ad5 can combine with Kupffer cell ablations to achieve systemic kinetics of virus particles with a half-life of >60 minutes, allowing ready access for peripheral tumor therapy, and that polymer-coating wild-type Ad5 can be used to deliver a replicative Ad5 systemically to tumors, with virus replication and transduction confined to tumor tissues and giving a much improved therapeutics index compared to uncoated virus.

tropism ablation and stealth technology combined with predosing strategies and Kupffer cell abalation allow systemic delivery of oncolytic Ad5 to tumors, with a half-life of more than 1 hour and a therapeutic index that is greatly improved over uncoated Ad5.

tropism ablation and stealth polymer coating of adenova type 5 (a vector used to deliver the gene for the therapeutic protein) can enhance systemic delivery of the therapeutic protein to tumors and improve the virotherapy of human hepatocellular carcinoma.

the use of oncolytic virus to treat cancer and we have developed a novel polymer-coating technology that has been shown to enhance the systemic delivery and therapeutic efficacy of oncolytic Ad5.
the development of novel approaches to the treatment of cancer using oncolytic adenovi- ruses.
the development of a novel therapeutic strategy for the treatment of cancer using a combination of polymer coating, predosing, and Kupffer cell abation.

polymer coating of wild-type Ad5 can be used to improve virotherapy of tumors, and that the technology is ready for use in clinical trials.
polymer-coating technology can be used to deliver oncolytic virus to tumor tissues, and to improve the therapeutic index of virotherapy.
polymer coating and Kupffer cell ablated adenovirus can be safely delivered systemically, and is highly effective for virotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polymer coating Ad5 and predosing strategies can achieve systemic delivery of virus particles with a half-life of >60 min and that this can lead to complete control of tumor growth.
tropism ablation and stealth coating of oncolytic virus particles can combine to allow systemic delivery of therapeutic virus to tumors, giving an improved virotherapy of solid cancers.
tropism ablation and polymer coating of oncolytic virus is a highly effective strategy for systemic virotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to deliver oncolytic adenovi-ruses systemically and achieve tumor-specific replication, with a therapeutic index that can be controlled by the dose of polymer-coated virus.
polymer-coated virus can be used to achieve systemic virotherapy with a high therapeutic index.
the use of stealth and tropism ablation technologies can allow the safe systemic delivery of oncolytic viruses and that this approach may be a useful tool for cancer virotherapy.
